Subject: Attachable metadata & routing exception for HelixHealth POC

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As the HelixHealth POC exercises the session affinity routing we noticed a reproducible gap where custom attachable metadata headers (x-rdwd-meta-*) are being stripped at the gateway and not propagated into the runtime routing layer. When that header is missing the request falls back to default routing which results in a slower variant and ~2–3x higher tail latency for a subset of calls.

Attached are: mapped_headers.png (screenshot from our proxy showing the header present upstream), and proposed-mapping.csv (the header->route hint mapping Helix wants to use).

Ask: can Platform/Runtime:
- confirm whether we intentionally sanitize x-rdwd-meta-* headers at the edge (we suspect a conservative whitelist),
- and if so, provide a short-term escape hatch (API param or SDK toggle) that forces the route-hint to be honored for a given session while we negotiate secure mapping.

Why this matters: Helix is relying on per-session route hints to pin requests to their reserved variant for regulatory isolation. If we can’t preserve attachable metadata they will see inconsistent isolation and higher costs, which will block the committed Reserved Capacity discussion.

Proposed next steps:
1) Product decision: allow an opt-in pass-through flag for headers beginning with x-rdwd-meta- (security review required).
2) Runtime action: quick config flag on the gateway to stop stripping these headers for flagged accounts or routes (can be ephemeral).
3) Sales/CS: if we can get a temporary workaround for Helix this week, we can proceed to procurement.

I’m looping Marissa and Logan for prioritization and triage. Happy to hop on a short call.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0123

Thanks for the quick write-up and attachments. Short term we'd accept a per-account config or a query-param override. If you can give us a temporary safe flag and a target timeline I can escalate internally. We’re also happy to do a short shared-screen demo of the failing flows so your engineers can see the session-level mismatch.

Thanks for the context and the repro artifacts — good catch. Quick triage notes below.

Root cause (short): our gateway enforces a header whitelist to protect downstream metadata from untrusted clients; x-rdwd-meta-* was intentionally omitted when whitelist was tightened last quarter. That behavior is correct by default but we should support opt-in pass-through for enterprise accounts that complete a mapping/security review.

Short-term mitigation (48–72h):
- I can add a per-account gateway flag (edge config) to allow passthrough for any headers with prefix x-rdwd-meta-. This is a config toggle only (no runtime code change) and can be applied to Helix’s account/route.
- Risk: minimal — headers are still audited and we will log any mapping activity to the account audit trail. I’ll coordinate with Security for a quick rubber-stamp.

Medium-term (product roadmap):
- We should build a managed mapping table in Console: allow customers to declare which x-rdwd-meta-* keys are route hints, require owner attestations, and record audit logs. That will be part of the routing reliability epic (Q3 roadmap).
- Timeline: config toggle (canary) in 2–3 days; console mapping UX + audit is Q3 (design in July, engineering in August).

Next steps I will take today:
1) Create edge config toggle for Helix (apply to their account) and validate in integration environment.
2) Send a short runbook for Sales/CS with steps to confirm fix and minimal risk points.
3) Open a Console-UX ticket and assign to Marissa for prioritization (linking the deal).

Camila/Logan: if you can schedule a 30-min screen-share with Alice for EOD tomorrow, we’ll validate the passthrough and then promote the toggle to canary.
